items.question: What must the home page file be called, so web servers find it first?
items.explanation: Web servers, including GitHub Pages, look for index.html first. Use lowercase.

items.question: Why does the page need <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">?
options: It makes the page load faster
It makes the page fit phone screens instead of looking zoomed out
items.explanation: Without the viewport tag, phones pretend to be wide and shrink the page. The tag tells them to use the real screen width.

items.question: Type the attribute that lets the link <a href="#about"> jump to this section.
items.explanation: A link with href="#about" jumps to the element whose id is "about".

items.question: How many <h1> headings should the page have?
items.explanation: One <h1> says what the whole page is about. Sections use <h2>, and smaller items use <h3>.

items.question: Type the CSS function that reads a variable, so the text uses the accent color.
items.explanation: var(--accent) reads the value of the custom property --accent. Change the variable once and everything that uses it changes.

items.question: Which rule builds as many columns as fit, with each column at least 250px wide?
items.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr)) makes a responsive grid with no media queries: one column on a phone and more on a larger screen.

items.question: What does position: sticky with top: 0 do to the header?
options: Keeps it at the top of the screen while you scroll
items.explanation: A sticky element scrolls normally until it reaches the top, then it stays there.

items.question: What does "mobile first" mean?
options: The base CSS is for small screens, and @media (min-width) rules add changes for bigger screens
The site is built in a phone app
items.explanation: You design the small screen first, then add rules for larger screens. It keeps the phone version simple and fast.

items.question: How does the dark-mode button change the whole page?
options: It sets data-theme="dark" on the <html> tag, and the CSS variables get new values
It reloads the page from the server
It changes every element one by one
items.explanation: JavaScript only sets one attribute. The CSS rule :root[data-theme="dark"] gives the variables new values, and every rule that uses them changes.

items.question: Why is localStorage wrapped in try ... catch in the script?
options: Because storage can be blocked, and the page must still work
items.explanation: In private mode or with blocked cookies, localStorage can throw an error. try ... catch keeps the rest of the script running.

items.question: You name a GitHub repository dara.github.io (your username is dara). What is the address of your Pages site?
items.explanation: A repository named USERNAME.github.io is published at the short address https://USERNAME.github.io/.

items.question: Where do you find the Lighthouse quality checker?
options: In the browser tools (F12), in the Lighthouse tab
items.explanation: Lighthouse is built into Chrome and Edge. It scores Performance, Accessibility, Best practices and SEO.

items.question: Why should every have a meaningful alt text?
options: Screen readers read it aloud, and it shows if the picture cannot load
It is required to make a link
It makes the image load faster
items.explanation: The alt text describes the picture for people who cannot see it, and appears if the image fails to load.

items.question: Write the CSS for a class .grid that is a grid with an 18px gap and responsive columns that are at least 250px wide.
items.explanation: Use display: grid, gap, and repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...)).
